Gulls flew near the boat or sat on the water like ducks, and they stared at the men with black, bead like eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> One gull came down and tried to land on the captains head, but he did not dare to strike at it with the heavy rope. <break time="0.8s" /> Any sudden movement could have turned the boat over, so the captain gently waved the bird away with his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> The oiler and the correspondent took turns at the oars, and changing seats in that small boat was harder than stealing eggs from under a hen. <break time="0.8s" /> So carefully did they move that the boat hardly rocked, and each man rowed until his back and arms ached. <break time="0.8s" /> Late in the morning the captain, raising himself in the bow, said that he could see the lighthouse at Mosquito Inlet. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent, who was rowing, had to turn his head many times before he finally found the tiny thing on the horizon. <break time="0.8s" /> It looked like the point of a pin, and yet it showed the men that land was really out there.
